title: rom-weaver weave
description: Schema revision v1 for the distributable patching-workflow definition. Canonically named rom-weaver-weave.json (plain, stream-codec compressed as rom-weaver-weave.json.<gz|bz2|xz|zst>, or carried at the root of an archive alongside its patch/ROM members). rom-weaver also content-probes any *.json against this schema, so a differently named file that validates here is still recognized as a weave. This schema mirrors the RomWeaverWeave Rust type; unknown fields are rejected.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema reference so editors bind autocomplete/validation when this weave is hand-authored. Preserved verbatim by `weave create --from`; never required.

version.description: Weave schema version. This public schema writes and reads version 1.

rom.description: The input ROM the patch chain applies to. Omit entirely for a ROM-agnostic weave; include with only `checks` (no url/path) for a checks-only weave where the applying user supplies the ROM.

patches.description: Ordered patch chain: array order is the apply order. May be empty only when `cheats` is not.

cheats.description: Cheat selections this weave reproduces, in selection order. They are baked into the ROM after the patch chain. Optional: a weave without it is a plain patch recipe.

output.description: Defaults for the final patched output. Overridable by explicit CLI flags / webapp edits.

checks.description: Expected checksums (algorithm -> lowercase hex) and/or exact byte size.

checksums.description: Map of checksum algorithm to expected lowercase hex digest.

headerMode.description: ROM copier-header handling. `auto` (default) re-adds emulator-required format headers and drops junk copier headers; `keep` retains; `strip` removes.

rom.description: The one ROM the chain starts from: where to get it and how to recognize it. Omit it for a patch-only weave whose user supplies the ROM.

name.description: Display / output-naming file name. When the applying user supplies the ROM separately, a different logical basename produces an advisory warning. Defaults to the source's base name.

url.description: Download URL for the ROM. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Weave-relative path (an archive member when the weave ships inside an archive). Mutually exclusive with `url`.

checks.description: Expected checksums/size of the ROM itself (also verifies downloads). These describe the chain's INPUT.

patch.description: One patch step: its source, display metadata, and declared checks. Exactly one of url or path.

id.description: Stable patch-slot identity retained when the source file is replaced.

version.description: Author-controlled release version for this patch; distinct from the weave schema version.

name.description: Display name for the patch card.

description.description: Free-form description shown on the patch card.

optional.description: When true the patch starts DESELECTED; omitted/false means applied by default. Every patch remains toggleable.

url.description: Download URL for the patch. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Weave-relative path (an archive member when the weave ships inside an archive). Mutually exclusive with `url`.

inputChecks.description: Expected checksums/size of the ROM state this patch applies to, ONLY when it differs from `rom.checks` (a mid-chain step).

outputChecks.description: Expected checksums/size immediately after this patch is applied, ONLY when it differs from the weave's final `output.checks`.

basis.description: What this patch's input checks were authored against: `base` (the weave's rom - verified once up front; the patch's embedded checks are skipped when it runs mid-chain) or `previous` (the previous selected patch's output, the default). Omitted means previous/inferred. `basis: "base"` with omitted `inputChecks` relies on `rom.checks`; declaring it WITH `inputChecks` pins a specific variant. The escape hatch for checksumless formats (IPS) whose basis cannot be inferred.

cheat.description: One cheat selection. `id` names the record in the cheat database; `code` is a raw-code snapshot so the entry still applies when the database is absent.

id.description: Cheat database record ID. An exact description is also accepted, so a hand-authored weave can name a cheat the way `cheat list` prints it. Must not be blank.

source.description: Which database the ID belongs to, for example `libretro-database`.

revision.description: The database revision the selection was made against.

description.description: The cheat's description, as the database records it.

code.description: Raw code snapshot, so the entry still applies when the local cheat database is absent.

codeKind.description: Explicit decoder for the raw code snapshot.

optional.description: When true an unresolvable cheat is skipped and named in the report; omitted/false makes it fail the apply.

output.description: Defaults and expected result for the final patched output. Compression stays an apply-time choice.

name.description: Default output file name for the patched result.

checks.description: Expected checksums/size of the final output once the full default chain is applied.
